gaps.sentence: He is one of the best ___ (SCIENCE) in the field.
gaps.hint: plural person needed after 'one of the best'
gaps.explanation: 'One of the best' is followed by a plural noun for people: scientists.

gaps.sentence: The audience was ___ by her performance (CAPTIVE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ate forms the verb: captivate. The passive 'was ... by' needs the past participle 'captivated'.

gaps.sentence: The instructions were unclear, so I had to ___ them completely (WRITE).
gaps.hint: write again — unclear the first time (re-); base verb needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix re- means again: rewrite. A base verb is needed after 'had to'.

gaps.sentence: My grandfather is still very ___ for his age (ACT).
gaps.explanation: An adjective is needed after 'very': active (-ive). 'Activity' is a noun and 'actively' an adverb.

gaps.hint: verb needed with a singular subject (-ate)
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ate forms the verb: activate. The singular subject 'alarm' needs the -s form 'activates'.

gaps.sentence: The street market sells ___ fruit in summer (JUICE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -y forms the adjective: juicy fruit. A comparative or adverb cannot modify 'fruit'.

gaps.hint: negative adjective needed (-ish): not appropriate for an adult
gaps.explanation: 'Childish' is negative (silly, immature); 'childlike' is positive (innocent). The embarrassment shows the negative sense.

gaps.sentence: The old factory will be ___ into flats (MODERN).
gaps.hint: verb needed in the passive (-ise); past participle
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ise forms the verb: modernise. The passive 'will be' needs the past participle 'modernised'.
